blocking.section: Process and concurrency model / Goroutines; Listeners and protocols; Failure semantics / RZ-RT registry
blocking.issue: Nothing bounds per-Node concurrency, although the System overview promises 'Bounded everything'. The document says it owns the fixed defaults for header-read, idle and write timeouts and for the per-Node connection ceiling, but it never gives their values. net/http ships with ReadHeaderTimeout 0 and no connection cap, so Slowloris or a connection flood grows goroutines and buffers without limit. Streaming and pass-through requests reserve nothing from maxBufferedBytes. RZ-RT-005 is defined for a 'concurrency ceiling' that the current answer to OQ-data-plane-6 says does not exist.
blocking.evidence: Line 140: "Header-read, idle and write timeouts and a per-Node connection ceiling are not Gateway fields; Nodes apply fixed defaults owned by this document (OQ-data-plane-1)." Line 52: "| Request handler | One per request or HTTP/2 stream | Buffer budget, connection limits (OQ-data-plane-6) |". Line 460: "| RZ-RT-005 | 503 | Node overloaded: a bounded queue or concurrency ceiling is full (OQ-data-plane-6) |". Line 494: "(a) Buffer budget and breaker limits only (current)". System overview line 38: "Every queue, buffer, pool, retry, fan-out, retired snapshot and per-key bucket table (LRU) has a ceiling."
blocking.fix: Add rows to Bounded resources with concrete (target) defaults: ReadHeaderTimeout, IdleTimeout, WriteTimeout (streaming Routes clear it), the per-Node connection ceiling (a limiting net.Listener), HTTP/2 MaxConcurrentStreams per connection, and a Node-wide in-flight request ceiling that returns RZ-RT-005. Alternatively, change OQ-data-plane-6's current option to a fixed ceiling. State that Stream pump and Composition step goroutines count against it.

blocking.section: Process and concurrency model / Goroutines
blocking.issue: The claim of zero locks on the request path cannot be built with the listed mechanisms. A sharded map with an LRU bound has to change the LRU order and evict under a per-shard mutex. The bounded Plugin pool waits 'briefly', which needs a channel or semaphore. http.Transport locks internally on every idle-connection get and put.
blocking.evidence: Line 58: "No request waits on another Node or on Ruralz Control, and Node-local state takes no lock on the request path: the snapshot is an `atomic.Pointer`, counters and breaker state are atomics, Endpoint sets are copy-on-write, and local token buckets live in a sharded map with an LRU bound". Line 62: "an exhausted pool rejects with `RZ-PLG-<NNN>` after a brief wait".
blocking.fix: Restate the rule as: no global lock, no lock held across I/O or a State Store call, and only short per-shard critical sections. Name the bucket-table mechanism, for example per-shard mutexes with CLOCK or sampled eviction. Say that connection pools use the standard library's internal locking, and give the pool wait bound as a (target) number.

blocking.section: Configuration snapshots and hot reload / Why no in-flight request is dropped
blocking.issue: Reference-counted retirement, as written, has a load-then-increment race and a hot shared counter. A request loads the pointer and then increments the pinned count. In between, the loader can retire the snapshot, see zero, and close its pools and wazero instances, so the request runs on closed resources. One shared atomic counter that every request on every core touches causes cache-line contention at the seed latency budgets.
blocking.evidence: Line 357: "**Reference-counted retirement.** A retired snapshot, with the pools and Plugin instances only it uses, is freed when its pinned-request count reaches zero, never earlier; carried-over pools are shared by reference." Line 356: "The request goroutine loads the snapshot pointer once, before routing". Figure 1: "L->>R: load the snapshot pointer once and pin it".
blocking.fix: Specify the pinning protocol: a striped or per-P counter incremented and then re-validated by re-loading the pointer, retrying if the snapshot was retired in between; the retirer marks the snapshot retired, then waits for the summed counts to reach zero. Alternatively, use epoch-based reclamation. Leave memory to the GC and apply explicit close only to pools and Plugin instances. Add a benchmark hook for the per-request pin cost.

blocking.section: Composition engine; Filter Chain execution / Streaming
blocking.issue: Reserving the worst case up front caps concurrency at implausibly low levels. A composition Route reserves its whole step body budget (up to 10 MiB by default) before the first step. With the 512 MiB default budget, one Node admits about 51 concurrent aggregate requests, and about 3 if decoded values (up to 4x) are also reserved. The request-body gate wording reads the same way for AI Routes and body-Phase Routes. Aggregation is KrakenD's core feature, and a parity workload would fail with RZ-RT-004.
blocking.evidence: Line 287: "and the Node reserves the step body budget from `limits.maxBufferedBytes` before the first step starts." Line 271: "a gate reserves bytes from `limits.maxBufferedBytes` before reading and fails with 503 `RZ-RT-004` when the reservation fails." Configuration model line 263: "512 MiB for `maxBufferedBytes`"; line 320: "at most 4 times the raw limit".
blocking.fix: Reserve incrementally as bytes arrive (for example 32 KiB increments), or reserve Content-Length when it is declared. Fail the gate or step at the point a reservation fails, with the existing codes and optional-step rules. Charge decoded values at decode time. State the resulting per-Node concurrency at the defaults as a (hypothesis) for Capacity planning.

blocking.section: Filter Chain execution / Streaming
blocking.issue: When onChunk is subscribed, chunk buffering has no bound and is left out of the Node budget. An SSE event has no size cap, so an Upstream that never terminates an event exhausts memory. A WebSocket message is capped only at 10 MiB per direction per stream (OQ-data-plane-5 option a) and is not reserved from maxBufferedBytes. LLM events have the same gap. 10,000 streams at 20 MiB each is 200 GiB.
blocking.evidence: Line 279: "A chunk is processed on its stream's goroutine and forwarded before the next is read, so the Node holds one chunk per direction beyond socket buffers". Line 276: "The message size cap is OQ-data-plane-5." Line 493: "(a) `limits.maxRequestBodyBytes` and `maxResponseBodyBytes` per direction (current)". Line 275: SSE "One chunk per event" with no cap.
blocking.fix: Cap every chunk kind (SSE event, WebSocket message, LLM event) with a small fixed (target) default, or a proposed field recorded in an Open question. Reserve each held chunk from maxBufferedBytes. On overflow, end the stream under closed semantics (SSE error event, WebSocket 1009 or 1011, RST_STREAM) with an RZ-RT code.

blocking.section: Configuration snapshots and hot reload / Why no in-flight request is dropped
blocking.issue: Closing a pinned HTTP/2 stream with GOAWAY cannot be built on net/http and would not release the snapshot. net/http has no public API for a handler to send GOAWAY on its own connection; only Server.Shutdown does, for every connection. A graceful GOAWAY also lets existing streams finish, so a long-lived gRPC or SSE stream stays pinned. The connection also carries streams on newer snapshots. The K bound therefore cannot be enforced for HTTP/2 streams. The System overview has the same sentence.
blocking.evidence: Line 359: "Activation never waits: when a third would be retired, long-lived streams pinned to the oldest get a graceful close (WebSocket 1001, HTTP/2 GOAWAY, or an SSE end with a retry hint), and short requests are unaffected."
blocking.fix: End the pinned stream itself: gRPC trailers with grpc-status UNAVAILABLE, stream reset (RST_STREAM through http.ErrAbortHandler) for other HTTP/2 streams, an SSE end event with a retry hint, WebSocket 1001. Add a bounded grace period (target) before the reset, and reflect it in the (K + 2) memory hypothesis.

blocking.section: Listeners and protocols
blocking.issue: RZ-RT-002 cannot be emitted as specified. When a request exceeds Server.MaxHeaderBytes, net/http writes its own plain-text 431 and closes the connection before any handler runs, so the RFC 9457 problem document with code and requestId never goes out. Also, MaxHeaderBytes is a field on a running http.Server, so changing it during a Hot Reload is a data race.
blocking.evidence: Line 134: "`limits.maxRequestHeaderBytes` sets `Server.MaxHeaderBytes`, and an oversized header block gets 431 with `RZ-RT-002`." Line 444: "A response the Node generates is an RFC 9457 problem document with media type `application/problem+json`, carrying the extension members `code` and `requestId`".
blocking.fix: Set Server.MaxHeaderBytes to a fixed process ceiling above the largest allowed Revision value, and enforce the Revision limit in the handler from the pinned snapshot so that RZ-RT-002 comes back as a problem document. Document the plain 431 above the ceiling. Treat other listener-level settings read from the snapshot the same way, or rebind them through the SO_REUSEPORT handover.

blocking.section: Configuration snapshots and hot reload
blocking.issue: The snapshot is immutable yet holds the Consumer API-key hash index, while secretRef-held keys are hashed at load and secrets rotate without a new Revision. A rotated key either waits for the next Revision or requires mutating an immutable snapshot. Both break a stated rule.
blocking.evidence: Line 336: "A snapshot is the compiled, immutable form of one Revision: Routers, Filter Chains, CEL programs, Plugin pool handles, Upstream settings, the Consumer credential index (API key hashes only) and TLS settings. Resolved secrets live in a separate in-memory store keyed by `secretRef`, which survives Hot Reloads and rotates without a new Revision." Configuration model line 485: "A retrievable key uses `secretRef`; the Node hashes it at load and keeps only the hash in memory".
blocking.fix: Keep hashes of secretRef-held keys in a runtime index beside the secret store, swapped copy-on-write on rotation (like Endpoint sets), with the snapshot holding only literal hashes and references. Alternatively, state that rotation atomically republishes the derived index. State that TLS certificates come from the secret store at handshake (GetCertificate).

The Configuration model says a Policy.spec.when error runs the Policy under closed and skips it under open, and that a cache key error bypasses the cache whatever the failureMode.

blocking.section: Process and concurrency model / Bounded resources; Failure semantics / RZ-RT registry
blocking.issue: No deadline covers work that happens before the Route is fixed. The only read and write deadline is the Route `timeout`, and server ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout are left unset. That leaves four Node-generated responses with no deadline: 503 RZ-RT-005 (in-flight ceiling full, before routing), 431 RZ-RT-002, 404 RZ-RT-001 and 500 RZ-RT-006. In Go's HTTP/2 server, a handler's final DATA write waits for flow-control window, so a client that advertises a zero stream window blocks the handler forever. IdleTimeout does not apply while streams are open. The attack: about 80 HTTP/2 connections x 250 streams, each sending a request to an unmatched path, hold all 20,000 in-flight units (target) and their snapshot pins with no time limit. From then on, every legitimate request on the Node gets 503 RZ-RT-005. The streams that go over the ceiling also block while writing their 503, so their goroutines and decoded header blocks (up to 256 KiB each) pile up outside every stated bound. Each held pin also forces every closing snapshot to wait out its full grace period.
blocking.evidence: "| Body reads and response writes | The Route `timeout`, set per request through `http.ResponseController`; server `ReadTimeout` and `WriteTimeout` unset |"; "| In-flight units per Node | 20,000 (target): one per request, parallel step and stream pump, taken by an atomic add; when full, 503 `RZ-RT-005` at once, never queued |"; "| RZ-RT-001 | 404 | No Route matched on this listener |"; Figure 1: "L->>L: admit under connection and in-flight ceilings, read headers" before "L->>R: pin the active snapshot".
blocking.fix: Add a Bounded resources row: at admission, every request gets fixed read and write deadlines through `http.ResponseController`, for example 10 s (target). The Route `timeout` replaces them once the Route is fixed. Node-generated responses written before routing, and any RZ-RT-005 rejection, use a short write deadline, for example 5 s (target). When a deadline expires, Go's HTTP/2 server resets the stream and the HTTP/1.1 server closes the connection. Say that this also bounds the goroutines of streams rejected with RZ-RT-005.

blocking.section: Configuration snapshots and hot reload / Why no in-flight request is dropped
blocking.issue: Ending pinned work at the end of the grace period has no mechanism that works as written, and the state machine contradicts the pin rule. First, only the handler goroutine can raise `http.ErrAbortHandler`. A handler blocked in a response write (HTTP/2 flow control, or a slow HTTP/1.1 reader), a body read or a wazero guest call cannot reach the panic, and cancelling a context the handler derived does not unblock a write in net/http. Wazero stops a running guest on cancellation only with `WithCloseOnContextDone`, which the research file reports costs a 10-20x slowdown on loop-heavy guests. Second, Figure 4 frees a closing snapshot when its grace period ends even if pins remain. That contradicts 'no request runs on a freed snapshot'. It lets the retirer close pools and Plugin instances that live goroutines are still using. It also breaks the (K + 2) memory bound, because the pending Revision compiles as soon as the closing snapshot counts as freed, while goroutines that have not unwound still hold it reachable.
blocking.evidence: "After a grace period of 30 s (target), anything still pinned ends with `RZ-RT-014`: 503 before commit, else `RST_STREAM` through `http.ErrAbortHandler` on HTTP/2 or a connection close on HTTP/1.1"; "The retirer swaps the pointer, then waits for the stripes to sum to zero, so no request runs on a freed snapshot."; Figure 4: "Closing --> Freed: pins reach zero or grace period ends"; "Because a pending Revision compiles only after the closing snapshot is freed, peak configuration memory is (K + 2) times the snapshot size (hypothesis)."; research go-libraries-runtime.md: "Open issue #2466 (2026-01-11) reports a 10–20x slowdown on loop-heavy guests with it enabled".
blocking.fix: Specify the termination protocol. At the end of the grace period, the retirer: (1) cancels each pinned request's root context, which aborts Upstream and State Store I/O; (2) sets past read and write deadlines through that request's `http.ResponseController`, which unblocks client I/O by resetting the HTTP/2 stream or closing the HTTP/1.1 connection; (3) relies on the Plugin call time limit for guest calls, naming the owner (WASM plugin system) and the bound. Then it waits for the pins to reach zero, bounded by that limit plus a small margin (target). Change Figure 4 so that the grace-period edge goes to an 'Ending' state and only 'pins reach zero' leads to Freed. Close resources only at zero pins, and state the (K + 2) bound under that rule. Note that concurrent use of `ResponseController` from the retirer needs a per-request mutex or a watchdog goroutine owned by the request.

blocking.section: Process and concurrency model / Bounded resources
blocking.issue: The per-connection memory figure leaves out the HTTP/2 frame read buffer, so the 32 GiB fit is wrong at the stated ceilings. The document sets the HTTP/2 receive buffers but leaves `HTTP2Config.MaxReadFrameSize` at Go's server default of 1 MiB. Flow control does not cover HEADERS, CONTINUATION or unknown frame types, so any client can make each connection's framer allocate a 1 MiB read buffer, and the framer keeps it for reuse. That is about 19.5 GiB across 20,000 connections (hypothesis). Added to the stated about 18 GiB, the total is about 37.5 GiB plus snapshots, which exceeds the 32 GiB Node. The row also leaves out the two goroutine stacks each HTTP/2 connection runs (serve and frame reader).
blocking.evidence: "| Per-connection memory | About 560 KiB before a handler runs (hypothesis): header ceiling, HTTP/2 connection receive buffer, and 48 KiB of TLS and `bufio` buffers |"; "Worst-case Node memory sums connections at 560 KiB (about 10.7 GiB), ... about 18 GiB plus snapshots, fitting a 32 GiB Node (hypothesis)"; "| HTTP/2 unread request data | `HTTP2Config.MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection` 256 KiB and `MaxReceiveBufferPerStream` 64 KiB (target) ([source](https://go.dev/doc/go1.24)) |"
blocking.fix: Add `HTTP2Config.MaxReadFrameSize` 16 KiB (target), the protocol minimum, to the HTTP/2 rows and to the per-connection sum. Add the connection goroutine stacks, for example 16 KiB (hypothesis). Then recompute the 560 KiB figure and the Node total, or lower the connection ceiling.

non_blocking.suggestion: Streams can now borrow the general budget without limit ('from the stream share, then free general budget'), which reverses the old coupling. About 400 WebSocket clients, each trickling a 1 MiB message, hold the 384 MiB general budget for the Route `timeout`, and every gate on the Node then fails with RZ-RT-004. Traffic management recommends 1 h timeouts for streaming Routes. Streams that stall mid-chunk while waiting on each other's partial reservations are also a hold-and-wait pattern that resolves only at the Route timeout. Cap what streams can borrow, for example growing only from the stream share, or letting borrowed bytes total at most a fixed fraction of the general budget (target).

blocking.section: Control Store and high availability
blocking.issue: Nothing fences stale replicas. A follower cut off from the leader stays ready, keeps serving Control Streams and keeps sending its last committed assignments. Its committed state can be older than what the majority has since committed, for example a completed Rollout, a rollback or a revocation. A Node that reconnects to that follower is sent an older assignment. It can regress to a superseded Revision, or re-activate one that was rolled back. A revoked certificate is still accepted at the handshake. Nodes cannot detect this, because Snapshot, Delta and HeartbeatReply carry no monotonic assignment sequence. The proposed regional relay (Planned (M4)) has the same hazard.
blocking.evidence: "Quorum loss stops writes only (TB-11): followers keep serving the last committed assignments and reads, and writes fail with `RZ-CP-004`." / "it does not fail on quorum loss or a missing leader, because followers still serve Control Streams" / "A reconnecting Node receives the Revision its persisted plan assigns, so reconnect storms cannot bypass a canary." / "`ruralz node revoke` records the revocation; replicas refuse the certificate at the handshake"
blocking.fix: Add a fencing rule. Every Snapshot, Delta, TrustUpdate and HeartbeatReply carries `assignmentIndex`, the Raft index of the entry that set that Node's assignment. The Node persists the highest index it has activated and sends a transient NACK for any configuration message with a lower index. A replica that has not heard from a leader within one election timeout (hypothesis) sends no new Snapshot or Delta. It answers Hello with nothing and HeartbeatReply with its last promoted digest only, and reports in a metric that it is stale. Add `assignmentIndex` to the message table and state that the regional relay follows the same rule. If this needs a new field in a Configuration model-owned schema, record it as an Open question.

blocking.section: Components
blocking.issue: The document never says how replicas coordinate. Streams end on every replica, but the Rollout engine, the gates, the Drift detector and the Node count run only on the leader. Heartbeat state lives only in the memory of the replica that serves the stream. The document leaves five things open. (a) How ACKs, NACKs, per-Revision heartbeat counters and connected-Node counts from followers reach the leader. `clusterNodeCount`, which sets derived Rate Limit ceilings (pack 8.8), needs every replica's streams. (b) Whether followers send Snapshots and Deltas themselves from committed assignments. Figure 1 shows only a local `ro --> cs` edge. (c) What a new leader does mid-canary with no heartbeat counters. A gate can pass or fail on empty data. (d) Which replica signs Enrollment and renewal certificates. Enroll and renewal can land on any replica, and token consumption is a Raft write. (e) Which 8092 connection class carries content replication and fetch-by-digest. Gates, Drift and ceilings all depend on this hidden path, and the document gives it no rate, bound or failure behavior.
blocking.evidence: "Every replica serves the REST API, Ruralz Console and Control Streams; only the Raft leader runs the Git watcher, Rollout engine and Drift detector." / "Heartbeats, sessions, stream state | Memory of the serving replica; rebuilt on reconnect" / "the leader evaluates it on every heartbeat aggregate" / "whose mutual-TLS stream layer tags each connection as Raft traffic or leader forwarding"
blocking.fix: Add an H3 'Replica roles' under Components with five rules. (1) Every replica sends configuration to its own Nodes from Raft-committed per-Node assignments. (2) Followers forward Ack and Nack to the leader at once. They send heartbeat aggregates (per Node: digests, ready, per-Revision counters, connected state) every 5 s (target) through a bounded per-follower queue that drops the oldest entries and counts the drops. (3) The leader computes `clusterNodeCount` from those aggregates with stated hysteresis. (4) Enrollment and renewal are forwarded to the leader, which consumes the token and signs, and fail with `RZ-CP-004` when there is no leader. (5) 8092 has tagged classes: Raft, write forwarding, status forwarding and content replication. After a leader change, the new leader restarts every open gate window, requests a full status resync from each replica and evaluates no gate until it holds data from every canary Node. Update Figure 1 to show these edges.

blocking.section: Control Stream
blocking.issue: Memory on the replica and on the Node is unbounded. Snapshots are chunked and capped at 32 concurrent, but Deltas are single messages with no size cap and bypass the limit. Each stream may queue 4 messages. Once Deltas reach Snapshot-chunk size, a change sent to 5,000 streams (hypothesis) on one replica holds about 5,000 x 4 x 1 MiB, roughly 20 GiB. The document sets no connect read or send limits, so one oversized Delta or EnrollResponse can also exceed message limits or force large allocations on the Node. The Node has no stated maximum for Snapshot `totalBytes`, which a buggy replica could exploit.
blocking.evidence: "At most 32 concurrent full snapshots per replica (target); deltas bypass the limit." / "Snapshot chunks are at most 1 MiB (target)" / Delta row: "`nonce`, `baseDigest`, `digest`, `ops` (add, replace, remove by identity), `signature`, `promotedDigest`" / "HTTP/2 flow control plus a per-stream send queue of 4 messages (target)"
blocking.fix: Cap an encoded Delta at 1 MiB (target). Send a larger change as a chunked Snapshot, which counts against the snapshot limit. Encode each Snapshot's chunks and each (base, target) Delta once, and share the immutable buffers across streams. Add a per-replica budget for bytes in flight (for example 256 MiB (target)) that covers Snapshots and Deltas together. Set connect `ReadMaxBytes` and `SendMaxBytes` on both ends. Give the Node a maximum `totalBytes`, above which it sends a deterministic NACK.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle
blocking.issue: The design contradicts its own 1 MiB Raft entry limit. The Revision's Raft entry embeds the `ruralz.diff.v1` JSON, which grows with the change and has no bound, so a large refactor or a Gateway Policy edit that touches hundreds of Routes can exceed 1 MiB. Persisted per-Node plans and ACK sets also live in Raft metadata. At the 10,000-Node target (target), a plan listing each Node's ULID (26 bytes) and full digest (71 bytes) is close to 1 MB before encoding overhead. Raft-committed data therefore does not stay small, and snapshot, restore and replication costs grow with change size.
blocking.evidence: "then commits one Raft entry with the digest, source commit, Bundle path, Environment, `ruralz.diff.v1` JSON against the previous Revision, and signature" / "Raft entries stay under 1 MiB (target) because content lives in the content store" / "Rollout records, persisted plans, ACK sets | Raft metadata; ACKs coalesced every 250 ms (target)"
blocking.fix: Store the diff JSON and the per-Node plan as content-store objects by digest, replicated to a quorum first, so Raft entries hold only their digests. Encode the plan compactly: canary and batch membership as the stable-hash rule plus batch boundaries, with one digest per batch rather than one per Node. Commit ACKs as incremental entries (plan-index bitmaps) instead of rewriting the set. State the resulting largest entry size as a (target).

blocking.section: Audit and security
blocking.issue: Audit and authentication state contradict the stated availability. (a) Entries accumulate into segments of up to 4 MiB, and only the chain head is committed through Raft. Entries in a segment that has not been sealed are lost if the leader crashes, which breaks 'Every state change is audited'. (b) Logins are audited state changes, and a durable audit write needs quorum. During quorum loss nobody can log in, which contradicts 'quorum loss: reads only'. (c) Sessions live in the memory of the serving replica, yet every replica serves the REST API. Without sticky load balancing, a request that reaches another replica is unauthenticated, and any replica failover logs users out.
blocking.evidence: "Every state change is audited, including logins, token issuance, REST API writes, ..." / "Segments of at most 4 MiB (target) each carry their predecessor's digest, and the chain head is committed through Raft" / "Ruralz Console and the REST API (quorum loss: reads only)" / "Heartbeats, sessions, stream state | Memory of the serving replica; rebuilt on reconnect"
blocking.fix: Commit audit entries through Raft in coalesced batches (for example every 250 ms (target)) before the audited write returns. Seal 4 MiB segments into the content store only from committed entries. For quorum loss, choose one rule and state it: either existing sessions and API tokens keep working for reads while new logins fail with `RZ-CP-004`, or logins are spooled locally and appended, marked late, when quorum returns. Make sessions work on any replica, for example with a session-signing key held in the Control Store and short-lived signed session tokens, or require sticky routing and say so.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle
blocking.issue: Signing key rotation can stall forever or strand Nodes. Step 2 waits for every enrolled Node to ACK, so a detached, long-offline or decommissioned but unrevoked Node blocks rotation indefinitely. If an operator forces progress instead, a Node that was offline during steps 1 to 3 returns trusting only the retired key. It cannot verify a TrustUpdate or Revision signed by the new key, so it NACKs with RZ-CFG-033 forever. The document gives it no recovery path.
blocking.evidence: "(1) Add the new public key in a `TrustUpdate` signed by the current key. (2) After every enrolled Node ACKs, sign with the new key. (3) Retire the old key once no Node reports an active or Last-Known-Good digest it signed." / "A Node accepts only anchor sets signed by a key it already trusts"
blocking.fix: Base step 2 on connected, non-revoked Nodes. Exclude Nodes disconnected longer than a staleness bound (for example the 30-day certificate lifetime (target)) and list them on the Drift screen. Keep the ordered chain of TrustUpdates, each signed by its predecessor, in the Control Store. Send a returning Node every link after its newest trusted key, right after Hello and before any configuration. A Node older than the retained chain must re-enroll; link this to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-10.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle
blocking.issue: The gate windows do not fit how gate data arrives. Gates read counters only from heartbeats, which are sent every 15 s by default, and Ruralz Control MAY raise that interval under load. A 30 s batch gate window therefore sees at most two heartbeats per Node, and none once the interval exceeds 30 s, so the gate passes without data. The gate also has no minimum sample size, so a canary with almost no traffic passes the 5xx comparison. And it has no baseline when no Nodes remain on the previous Revision, such as a one-Node Cluster, the final batch or a 100% canary.
blocking.evidence: "Progressing batches | 25%, 25%, then the remaining 50% of non-canary Nodes (target), each followed by a 30 s gate window under `canary` (target)" / "Nodes send a heartbeat every 15 s (target), and Ruralz Control MAY raise `heartbeatInterval` under load." / "a canary 5xx ratio at most 1 percentage point above Nodes on the previous Revision (target)"
blocking.fix: Set each gate window to max(30 s, 3 x heartbeatInterval) (target), and never raise `heartbeatInterval` for Nodes in the active canary set or batch. Require a minimum number of requests per gate (for example 200 (target)). Below it, extend the window up to `canary.bake`, then apply a stated outcome: pass with a warning, or pause. When no baseline Nodes exist, compare against the previous Revision's recorded 5xx ratio from before the Rollout.

blocking.section: Ruralz Console
blocking.issue: The password-hashing choice conflicts with the Tech stack cryptography rule and with the FIPS build. The foundation pack and P1 give the FIPS build the same features. Tech stack G3 admits only Go `crypto/...` or `golang.org/x/crypto` packages that delegate to the Go Cryptographic Module, and anything else must be a named exception. The memory-hard KDFs in x/crypto (argon2, scrypt) do not delegate and are not FIPS-approved. Local accounts, the only identity source in M2, therefore cannot be built as written for the FIPS build (Planned (M5)), and the document has no G3 exception or Open question for it.
blocking.evidence: "In M2, identities are local accounts with salted, memory-hard password hashes and optional TOTP" vs Tech stack G3: "Cryptographic primitives come only from Go `crypto/...` or from `golang.org/x/crypto` packages that delegate to the Go Cryptographic Module in FIPS mode; anything else is a named exception"
blocking.fix: Replace 'memory-hard' with a KDF that works in both builds, such as PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from the Go standard library with a stated iteration count (target). Alternatively, keep memory-hard hashing in the default build only. Either way, add an Open question owned by tech-stack-and-libraries that decides the KDF and any named G3 exception, and name no library until a catalog row exists.

blocking.section: GitOps model
blocking.issue: An unapproved promotion deadlocks the Cluster. A `prod` Rollout is created in `pending` and waits there for `ruralz rollout approve`. A Cluster has at most one active Rollout, and newer builds wait in the newest-wins queue until the Cluster is free. `pending` has no exit except approval: rollback is defined only from `canary`, `progressing` or `paused`, and superseding is deferred to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-5, whose current option is 'finish or roll back first'. If an operator declines to approve commit A, for example because a fix B is already merged, B can never reach prod. The only way out is to approve A, ship it to canary Nodes, then roll it back. That is the risk the approval exists to prevent.
blocking.evidence: "`prod` gets one only after the commit's `staging` Revision reached `complete` in every `staging` Cluster, then waits in `pending` for `ruralz rollout approve`" / "Each Cluster has at most one active Rollout. Builds arriving meanwhile wait as a per-Cluster queue head where the newest wins, and a Rollout is created in `pending` only when the Cluster is free" / "During `canary`, `progressing` or `paused`" / Figure 3: "pending --> canary: strategy canary, approval given if required"
blocking.fix: Approve before creating the Rollout. A promotion awaiting approval stays as the Cluster's queue head, where newest-wins replacement still applies, and does not count as an active Rollout. `ruralz rollout approve` creates the Rollout in `pending`, which then proceeds at once. Update Figure 3, the promotion paragraph and `RZ-CP-006` to match. This keeps the seven pack 8.3 states and needs no pack amendment.

blocking.section: Control Store and high availability
blocking.issue: The `postgres` mode contradicts the coordination model the rest of the document relies on. Leader-only components (Git watcher, Rollout engine, Drift detector) and write forwarding exist only through Raft leadership and 8092. The `postgres` implementation 'leaves 8092 unused' and has no Raft leader, yet the document never says how a single Rollout engine is elected, how followers forward writes and status, or how content reaches peers. It says only 'behind the same interface'. As written, two replicas on `postgres` would both run the Rollout engine, or neither would.
blocking.evidence: "only the Raft leader runs the Git watcher, Rollout engine and Drift detector" / "Followers forward writes to the leader over the peer layer on 8092" / "The optional `postgres` implementation, Planned (M4), keeps metadata and content in PostgreSQL behind the same interface, leaves 8092 unused and waits on a driver selection (OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-20)"
blocking.fix: State that the Control Store interface includes leadership: under Raft, the Raft leader; under `postgres`, a lease held in PostgreSQL (for example a session advisory lock or a lease row with a fencing token), with renewal and expiry timing tagged (target). Say that under `postgres` every replica writes directly to PostgreSQL, so no write forwarding is needed. Say that status forwarding goes through PostgreSQL or needs a peer channel, which this document must then define. If this cannot be decided now, add an Open question that blocks `postgres` (Planned (M4)).

non_blocking.suggestion: The body has about 4,852 words against the 5,000 maximum, so the blocking fixes will push it over. Cut words to make room, for example by shortening the Istio and xDS lead-in in Control Stream or folding the API resource table's CLI column into prose.

Cluster sequencing conflicts with the newest-wins per-Cluster queue. If commit B arrives while A is in progress on prod-eu-west, say whether prod-us-east later receives A (complete on eu-west) or B (not yet through canary on eu-west). State that a Cluster only receives a commit whose Revision reached `complete` on the previous Cluster, and what 'a failure stops the Environment there' means for the next commit.

Git divergence as defined fires on every normal promotion. A downstream Environment's promoted Revision differs from the branch-head render while the commit bakes upstream or waits for approval, and the alert escalates after one hour. Compare against the newest commit that is eligible for the Cluster under its promotion rules, not the branch head.

Define when a revert 'could not finish' (`failed`). Give a timeout or retry budget for re-delivering the previous Revision, and say how a Node that activated the new Revision and then went offline is counted: quarantined, or a cause of `failed`.

Define bootstrap for a Cluster with no promoted digest and for a Rollout planned with zero enrolled Nodes. 'At least one' canary Node is impossible then, and 'Late Nodes ... serve the promoted digest until then' leaves new Nodes not ready when no promoted digest exists.

Unary `Enroll` on 8091 runs without a client certificate while `Stream` requires one. State the TLS mode, for example `tls.VerifyClientCertIfGiven` with per-RPC enforcement that `Stream` presents a valid, unrevoked Node certificate, so the listener is buildable and TB-5 stays accurate.

Require nonces to be unique across replicas, for example by prefixing the replica ID and stream epoch, so `lastNonce` in Hello and 'stale nonces are ignored' stay correct when a Node moves between replicas. Also say whether `TrustUpdate` counts as the one unacknowledged configuration message.

blocking.section: Ruralz Console
blocking.issue: The RBAC model defeats the promotion approval it exists to enforce, and it contradicts itself. Roles are cumulative in list order, so `editor` includes `approver` and `operator`. One principal can therefore author a change (Console write-back or `ruralz bundle push`, which skips Git review) and approve its own `prod` promotion, which makes `requireApproval: true` meaningless. The screen table's single 'Minimum role' column also contradicts the role table: it gives `operator` for Nodes, Rollouts and Drift, `approver` for Environments and `admin` for Settings, while `viewer` may 'Read every screen except Access and the audit log', and the API summary lists `/api/v1/nodes` List at `viewer` but `/api/v1/rollouts` List at `operator`. The text never says whether `admin` can read the audit log, because `auditor` is excluded from inheritance. The sibling Security and identity document proposes `approver` 'never for its own change', a separate `security-admin` role for Enrollment tokens and revocation, and `viewer` reading the audit log. An operator or security reviewer cannot configure least privilege from this section.
blocking.evidence: RBAC and SSO: "Roles are built in and bound globally or per Environment; each includes the roles listed before it, except `auditor`, which only reads audit data." Role table: "| viewer | Read every screen except Access and the audit log |" and "| editor | Ruralz Console write-back and `ruralz bundle push` |". Screen table: "| Nodes | ... | Issue Enrollment token; revoke (admin) | operator |" and "| Rollouts | ... | Start, pause, resume, roll back | operator |". API summary: "| `/api/v1/rollouts` | List, start; pause, resume, rollback, approve | ... | operator; approver to approve |".
blocking.fix: Remove `approver` from the inheritance chain so no other role includes it. Add the rule 'an approver cannot approve a promotion whose source commit, write-back or pushed Bundle they authored; the attempt is RZ-CP-007 and is audited'. Split 'Minimum role' into 'View' and 'Act' columns, with `viewer` under View for every screen except Access and Audit log, and make API list and read operations `viewer` throughout. State whether `admin` includes `auditor`. Either align role names with Security and identity (`security-admin` for Enrollment tokens, revocation and trust anchors) or record the difference as an Open question owned by security-and-identity.

blocking.section: GitOps model; Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle
blocking.issue: An unapproved promotion blocks the Cluster, and the approval unit is undefined. A `prod` Rollout is created in `pending` and waits there for `ruralz rollout approve`, and each Cluster has at most one active Rollout. Figure 3 and pack 8.3 give `pending` no exit except to `canary` or `progressing`: no rollback, cancel or reject, and no cancel verb exists. If an approver rejects the commit, or a newer commit supersedes it, the Cluster stays blocked unless someone approves a Revision they do not want. OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-5 covers only superseding an in-flight Rollout. The text also leaves open whether approval is given once per promotion (commit and Environment) or once per Cluster Rollout. Clusters of an Environment roll out one at a time, so `prod-us-east`'s Rollout is created only after `prod-eu-west` completes. Does it wait in `pending` for a second approval? Approvers and operators cannot predict the workflow.
blocking.evidence: Branch-to-Environment mapping: "while `prod` gets one only after the commit's `staging` Revision reached `complete` in every `staging` Cluster, then waits in `pending` for `ruralz rollout approve`." Building and recording a Revision: "Each Cluster has at most one active Rollout. Builds arriving meanwhile wait as a per-Cluster queue head where the newest wins, and a Rollout is created in `pending` only when the Cluster is free". Figure 3: "pending --> canary: strategy canary, approval given if required". Multi-cluster: "after that Rollout completes and approval is given, `prod` proceeds with `prod-eu-west`, then `prod-us-east`."
blocking.fix: Model approval as an Environment-level promotion record (source commit or pushed tree digest, Environment) that sits in the newest-wins queue before any Rollout exists. `ruralz rollout approve` approves the promotion once for every Cluster of the Environment. A newer eligible commit replaces an unapproved one, and a rejected promotion is discarded, which needs either a reject action (a new verb through a pack section 9 amendment) or an explicit Open question. Create each Cluster's `pending` Rollout only after approval, and state that `pending` then lasts only until the plan is dispatched. Update the labels in Figure 3 and the Environments screen to match.

blocking.section: Drift detection
blocking.issue: The Git divergence rule flags normal promotion as Drift. A downstream Environment's promoted Revision always differs from the branch-head render while the commit bakes upstream or waits for approval, and so does any Cluster during its own Rollout or while it waits for an earlier Cluster in the lexical order. This happens on every merge and can last for days on `prod`. Because divergence older than one hour raises severity, every ordinary approval wait turns into an escalating alert. Operators cannot tell real divergence (break-glass `ruralz rollout start`, a pushed Bundle, a CRD source) from a queued promotion, so the reconciliation policy that acceptance criterion 5 asks for is not usable as written.
blocking.evidence: Drift table: "| Git divergence | A Cluster's promoted Revision differs from the one rendered from the branch head, such as after a break-glass `ruralz rollout start` or a pushed Bundle | Drift screen with age, audit event, metric | Alert only; never reverted automatically, since it may be deliberate |" and "Git divergence older than one hour raises severity (target)."
blocking.fix: Define Git divergence against the Revision the promotion chain currently entitles the Cluster to: the newest commit that passed `promotion.from` and approval. Report 'awaiting promotion', 'awaiting approval' and 'queued behind Cluster X' as promotion or Rollout status, not as Drift. Count as divergence only Revisions whose source is not the entitled commit (break-glass, pushed Bundles, CRD sources), and start the one-hour severity clock only for those.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle
blocking.issue: Operators cannot act on the most common incident rollback: a Revision that passed its canary, reached `complete` and then misbehaves. The only fast path is break-glass `ruralz rollout start` with the previous Revision. The document never says whether that Rollout is subject to `promotion.from` and `requireApproval` (so it could wait in `pending` for an approver during an incident), whether the Cluster's `canary.bake` (15m in the example) and the 30 s batch windows apply, which role may run it, or which Revisions are eligible. The Git path (revert, merge, staging bake, approval, then Cluster by Cluster) takes hours. The operator cannot estimate time to recovery or confirm permissions from this section.
blocking.evidence: Rolling back in three steps: "A `complete` Rollout is terminal: revert the commit in Git, or, as break-glass, `ruralz rollout start` with the previous Revision, which Drift reports as diverging from Git until the revert merges."

blocking.section: Control Stream
blocking.issue: Disposable Nodes (P4) are not operable in Control mode. Each Node needs its own single-use, one-hour Enrollment token, which an operator issues by hand in Figure 4. An autoscaled or Kubernetes-managed Cluster cannot scale out or replace a pod without an undescribed automation that holds a token-minting credential. A replacement pod without a persistent `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` gets a new identity, and the old one is never cleaned up. The published Node count is never defined as connected, ready or enrolled Nodes. It sets derived per-Node Rate Limit ceilings (pack 8.8), so stale identities would silently shrink every ceiling, and signing-key rotation step 2 waits on 'every enrolled Node'. Operators cannot run horizontal scaling from this document.

Tag any interval (target).

blocking.section: Ruralz Console / RBAC and SSO; GitOps model / Ruralz Console write-back; API summary
blocking.issue: Roles are cumulative, so one principal can author, push and approve its own production change. `editor` inherits `approver` and `operator`. With a phished account or leaked CI token, an attacker runs `ruralz bundle push` for staging and then prod, bypassing Git review. Promotion gating is met because the same source tree digest completed staging. The same principal then runs `ruralz rollout approve`, which defeats `requireApproval`. `operator` can also issue Enrollment tokens, so any Rollout operator can enroll a rogue Node.
blocking.evidence: Line 467: "each includes the roles listed before it, except `auditor`". Line 472: "operator | ... issue Enrollment tokens". Line 474: "editor | Ruralz Console write-back and `ruralz bundle push`". Line 202: "records the source tree digest in place of a commit, so promotion gating applies". Line 439: "Alert only; never reverted automatically". 08-security-and-identity.md line 433: "`approver` ... never for its own change".
blocking.fix: Make roles non-cumulative capability sets, or at least stop `editor` from inheriting `approver`. Enforce separation of duties on the server: reject `ruralz rollout approve` with RZ-CP-007 when the approver authored or merged the commit, pushed the source Bundle, or started the Rollout. Make `ruralz bundle push` a per-Environment permission that is off by default where `requireApproval` is set. Move Enrollment tokens to a dedicated role. Add a threat row for a compromised editor account or CI token.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle / Revision signing and verification; Rolling back in three steps; API summary
blocking.issue: Nothing binds a signed Revision to its Environment or Cluster. Nodes never compare the signed Environment name with their own. `ruralz rollout start` (operator) accepts any Revision, and the document never says whether gating and approval apply. A validly signed staging Revision, which may relax auth, can therefore be rolled out to prod. The break-glass path has no role, reason or eligibility rule.
blocking.evidence: Line 256: "Signed content | The full `sha256:<64 hex>` digest, Environment name, key ID and signing time". Line 259: Node verification checks only the digest and the signature. Line 323: "as break-glass, `ruralz rollout start` with the previous Revision". Line 519: "`/api/v1/rollouts` | List, start ... | operator".
blocking.fix: (1) Ruralz Control refuses a Rollout, with a new RZ-CP code, whose Revision Environment differs from `Cluster.spec.environment`. (2) A Node NACKs, with RZ-CFG-033, a Revision whose signed Environment differs from the Environment bound to its Enrollment certificate. (3) An explicit-Revision start is limited to Revisions that earlier reached `complete` in that Cluster; anything else goes through the normal gates. Break-glass needs `admin` or a dedicated role and a reason, and is audited as its own event type.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle / Revision signing and verification; Control Stream (message table)
blocking.issue: Revision signatures have no freshness and no anti-rollback property. Old signed Revisions, such as one with a rotated key hash, a vulnerable Plugin or a disabled `authz` Policy, can be replayed by a compromised follower, the relay, a MITM (L4S-12) or a stale restore (L4S-13). `promotedDigest` and `rolloutId` are unsigned.
blocking.evidence: Line 256 (the signed content has no sequence or expiry). Line 336: "`Snapshot` | ... `signature`, `promotedDigest`, `rolloutId`". Line 341: "`HeartbeatReply` | ... `promotedDigest`". Line 429: the relay "caches Revision content by digest".
blocking.fix: Add a leader-signed assignment for each delivery over (Cluster, digest, Rollout ID, monotonic per-Cluster sequence, expiry), and sign `promotedDigest` the same way. Nodes persist the highest sequence under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/identity/` and reject a lower, equal or expired one. A rollback becomes a new, higher-sequence assignment. Add a threat row for replay.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle / Revision signing and verification; Audit and security
blocking.issue: The online Revision signing key also signs `TrustUpdate`. If it is stolen (the key-encryption key sits on every replica), the attacker can install their own anchors and lock the legitimate Ruralz Control out permanently. There is no emergency revocation or compromise-recovery path.
blocking.evidence: Line 258: "Encrypted in the Control Store under a key-encryption key from process configuration". Line 262: "(1) Add the new public key in a `TrustUpdate` signed by the current key. (2) After every enrolled Node ACKs...". Line 264: "A Node accepts only anchor sets signed by a key it already trusts". Line 561: "It can deliver anything its key signs".
blocking.fix: Use a separately held trust-root key, pinned at Enrollment through the token, as the only `TrustUpdate` signer. The online key signs only Revisions and assignments. Add root-signed emergency key removal that does not wait for ACKs. Name re-enrollment as the recovery path if the root is lost. Add threat rows for theft of the signing key and of the key-encryption key.

blocking.section: Control Stream (message table); Rollout plan, batches and gates; Audit and security
blocking.issue: One compromised Node can veto every Rollout by sending a `Nack` with `class: deterministic`, which the design trusts. A canary Node can also fake healthy gate counters. The threat table understates the impact of a stolen Node certificate.
blocking.evidence: Line 339: "Deterministic fails the gate at once". Line 280: "Gates read per-Revision request, 5xx and rejection counters that Nodes send in heartbeats". Line 554: "Stolen Node certificate | Sees only its Cluster's Revisions".
blocking.fix: Ruralz Control reproduces a claimed deterministic NACK with its own validation library before failing the gate. A NACK that does not reproduce becomes transient, and the Node is quarantined with an alert. Bound one Node's weight in gate decisions and treat per-Node counters as outlier signals. Rewrite the threat row.

blocking.section: Control Stream / Enrollment and mTLS; message table and backpressure
blocking.issue: Nodes supply their own `nodeId`. Nothing requires uniqueness, a match between `Hello` and the certificate, or a fixed subject on renewal CSRs, so a token holder can take over an existing Node's identity. The unauthenticated `Enroll` RPC has no rate, size or lockout limits, and RZ-CP-001 versus RZ-CP-002 reveals whether a token exists.
blocking.evidence: Line 333: "`EnrollRequest` ... `token`, `nodeId`, `csr` ... the token is consumed only on success". Line 335: "`Hello` | ... `nodeId`". Line 343: "`RenewRequest` ... `csr`". Line 384: "A token bucket on new streams per replica".
blocking.fix: Enforce `node.id` uniqueness at Enrollment. Take identity only from the verified certificate and reject a mismatched `Hello`. Renewal CSRs keep the same `node.id` and Cluster. Reject any `Stream` without a client certificate. Add a per-source bucket, a maximum message size and lockout for `Enroll`, and return one external error for all token failures.

blocking.section: GitOps model; Components (CRD watcher); Audit and security
blocking.issue: CRDs produce Revisions with undefined authorization and audit. Any Kubernetes principal allowed to write `ruralz.io` objects bypasses RBAC, review and audit. The document does not say the path is off by default.
blocking.evidence: Line 122: "CRD watcher | Assembles `ruralz.io/v1alpha1` CRDs into a Bundle per namespace". Line 133: "Revisions come only from Git, `ruralz bundle push` or CRDs". Line 549: the audit list omits CRD changes.
blocking.fix: Turn the CRD source off by default and enable it only by a namespace-to-Environment binding in process configuration. Ignore `Environment` and `Cluster` CRDs without that binding. Audit the Kubernetes user of each change, and have Drift report CRD-sourced Revisions as not from Git. Add a threat row.

blocking.section: Multi-cluster and multi-region sync; Audit and security
blocking.issue: The proposed read-only relay has no trust model. It can forge ACKs and heartbeats for its whole Region, advance the promoted digest, hide Drift, replay Revisions and withhold revocations. Yet the document claims no unauthenticated crossing.
blocking.evidence: Line 429: the relay "terminates its Region's Node streams, caches Revision content by digest, forwards ACK batches and heartbeat aggregates". Line 563: "this design adds no unauthenticated crossing".
blocking.fix: Give the relay its own certificate class with an allowed-Cluster list and a revocation command, and no signing power. Nodes verify signatures end to end. Either declare the relay trusted for its Region's ACKs or have Nodes sign ACKs and heartbeats. The relay enforces revocations. Add a threat row.

blocking.section: Ruralz Console / RBAC and SSO
blocking.issue: Memory-hard password hashing (argon2 or scrypt from x/crypto, which does not delegate to the Go Cryptographic Module) contradicts tech-stack G3, which has no named exception for it, and breaks FIPS-build parity (P1). There is no login throttling or lockout, and TOTP is optional even for `admin`.
blocking.evidence: Line 478: "local accounts with salted, memory-hard password hashes and optional TOTP". 01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md line 38: "G3 | Cryptographic primitives come only from Go `crypto/...` or from `golang.org/x/crypto` packages that delegate to the Go Cryptographic Module in FIPS mode; anything else is a named exception".
blocking.fix: Name the algorithm: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 through `crypto/pbkdf2` with an iteration count (target), or argon2id in the default build and PBKDF2 in FIPS builds, the latter with an Open question for a G3 exception row. Add per-account and per-source throttling and lockout with audit events. Require TOTP or SSO for `admin` and `approver`.

blocking.section: Components; Change detection and pull request validation; Building and recording a Revision
blocking.issue: The online Plugin check makes the leader dial any registry host a Bundle author writes in `Plugin.spec`. That is SSRF from the most privileged process: metadata endpoints, 9902 or internal services. Registry credential scoping is undefined.
blocking.evidence: Line 101: "bld -.->|online Plugin check by digest| oci". Line 225: "validate, render per Environment, online Plugin check". Line 246: "runs every offline and online check".
blocking.fix: Add a registry allowlist in process configuration, with an Open question for an RZ-CFG diagnostic. Deny loopback, link-local, metadata and private ranges unless allowed. Bind each credential to its host with no forwarding across redirects. Cap size and time. Add a threat row.

blocking.section: GitOps model / Repository layout; Building and recording a Revision
blocking.issue: The document never says how symlinks, submodules or LFS pointers are handled. A committed symlink could pull leader-local files, such as process configuration with the key-encryption key or Git credentials, into the recorded source tree or its diagnostics. `viewer` can read that tree, and it ships to Nodes.
blocking.evidence: Line 246: "Recording writes the canonical JSON and source tree to the content store". Line 518: "`/api/v1/revisions` | List, get content ... | viewer".
blocking.fix: Read the Bundle and control directory straight from Git objects, with no working tree. Reject symlinks, gitlinks and LFS pointers, with an Open question for the RZ-CFG code, and apply the same rule in the CLI. Diagnostics never echo file content. Add a threat row.

blocking.section: Control Stream / Enrollment and mTLS; Components; Backup, restore
blocking.issue: The PKI is undefined. The document mentions an Enrollment CA, a server CA, `controlCa`, Ruralz Control's CA and a Node CA, but never says whether they are one CA, which CA signs the 8091 and 8092 certificates, or which EKU and SAN checks apply. If Node and server certificates share a CA, a stolen Node certificate can impersonate Ruralz Control to other Nodes.
blocking.evidence: Line 124: "Enrollment CA | Sign Revisions and Node certificates". Line 333: "server CA pinned by the token". Line 371: "fingerprint of Ruralz Control's CA". Line 509: "the Node CA is restored". Line 129: "Node certificates are rejected there."
blocking.fix: Add a certificate table: a Node client CA (clientAuth EKU only, SAN `node.id` plus Cluster), a pinned 8091 server identity (serverAuth, service SAN), a separate 8092 peer CA, and a relay class. Nodes verify the EKU and SAN. State key custody and rotation for each CA.

blocking.section: Control Store and high availability / Backup, restore and postgres; API summary
blocking.issue: Restoring an older backup brings back revoked Node identities, tokens, users and keys, and the document says Node certificates stay valid. `admin` can stream the archive, which holds encrypted keys and every credential hash, and restore it over REST. Archive integrity and confidentiality are unspecified.
blocking.evidence: Line 490: "Enrollment records, token hashes, revocations, encrypted CA and signing keys | Raft metadata | Yes". Line 509: "Node certificates stay valid because the Node CA is restored". Line 525: "`/api/v1/backup` | Stream a backup; restore ... | admin".
blocking.fix: A restore enters a restricted mode: it rejects certificates issued before a cut-over until they are checked against an exported revocation list, or requires re-enrollment. It invalidates sessions and API tokens and forces signing-key rotation before any Rollout. Sign and encrypt archives, audit downloads, and consider limiting restore to the host CLI.

blocking.section: GitOps model / Branch-to-Environment mapping; Repository layout; Multi-cluster and multi-region sync
blocking.issue: The gates are defined in the same repository they gate. One commit, or a Console write-back, can remove `requireApproval` or `promotion.from`, or move a Cluster's `spec.environment` to prod, and the change takes effect at once. What an approval binds to is undefined, and the newest-wins queue across sequential Clusters could deliver an unapproved newer commit.
blocking.evidence: Lines 147-149: `control/environments.yaml`, `clusters.yaml` in the same repository. Line 153: "Ingested `Environment` and `Cluster` resources pass the same validation library". Line 248: "per-Cluster queue head where the newest wins". Line 427: "after that Rollout completes and approval is given, `prod` proceeds with `prod-eu-west`, then `prod-us-east`".
blocking.fix: A gate-relaxing change to an `Environment` or `Cluster` gets impact `security`, applies only after an `approver` approves it, and never applies to the commit that introduces it. Record approvals against (Environment, commit, digest), and require a new approval when the queue head changes. Recommend separate forge review for `control/`.

blocking.section: Revision signing and verification; Control Stream (message table); Ruralz Console (Settings)
blocking.issue: Pack 8.14 requires the Plugin signature trust policy to be sent to Nodes over the Control Stream. The document defines only Revision `trustAnchors` and never says where the Plugin trust policy is configured or who changes it. Settings lets `admin` edit trust anchors outside Git, so a stolen admin session can trust an attacker's Plugin publisher. Node behavior when the policy is missing is unstated.

blocking.section: Control Stream
blocking.issue: The Node's fixed 128 MiB `totalBytes` cap contradicts the Configuration model's size rule. The Configuration model makes size limits configurable, proposes 64 MiB of source text and 20,000 resources, and promises that no Bundle that passes CI fails on a Node for size. A Snapshot carries the canonical form, in which every schema and registry default is materialized, and for large Bundles that can exceed the source size by a wide margin. An operator who raises the source limit also raises the snapshot size, but the Node's cap stays fixed. A Bundle that passes `ruralz bundle validate` and `build` can therefore produce a Revision that every Node NACKs deterministically with RZ-CFG-001, but only at Rollout time. The same size also fits the 256 MiB per-replica in-flight budget only twice. Neither Ruralz Control nor CI checks the encoded size before the Revision is recorded.
blocking.evidence: "Messages cap at 2 MiB (target); a `totalBytes` above 128 MiB (target) gets a deterministic NACK (RZ-CFG-001)." / "At most 32 concurrent Snapshots and 256 MiB in flight per replica (target)." vs Configuration model: "Size limits are configurable; exceeding one is RZ-CFG-001. The proposed defaults are 64 MiB of source text and 20,000 resources (target). A Node never enforces a limit below the CLI default, so no Bundle that passes CI fails on a Node for size."
blocking.fix: Make the encoded Revision size a build-time check. `ruralz bundle build` and the Ruralz Control builder reject, with RZ-CFG-001, any Revision whose Snapshot encoding exceeds the Node cap, so CI fails before merge and no Revision is recorded that Nodes would refuse. Derive the Node cap from the same configurable limit, never from a fixed value below the CLI default. Say that one Snapshot larger than the per-replica byte budget is admitted alone, not refused. If the Node cap needs a process setting or a field, add an Open question owned by configuration-model.

blocking.section: Multi-cluster and multi-region sync
blocking.issue: The regional relay (Planned (M4)) has no way to receive the state it serves. Replica role 5 allows relays on 8092 only 'status forwarding and read-only content fetch'. Both classes carry data from the relay to the leader, or content fetched by digest. Neither carries committed metadata to the relay. Per-Node assignments, promotions with their sequences, revocations, anchor sets and `clusterNodeCount` are Raft metadata, not content objects, and a relay is not a Raft member. The fencing rule also defines staleness as having no word from a leader, but no class gives a relay leader contact. As written, the relay cannot learn what to send, cannot enforce revocations and cannot tell whether it is stale. This document decides OQ-system-overview-16 with this relay design, so the gap is in a decision it owns.
blocking.evidence: "8092 authorizes tagged classes by certificate role ... Raft and write forwarding only from current Raft members; status forwarding and content replication between replicas; status forwarding and read-only content fetch for relays" / "It receives committed assignments and revocations, caches content, forwards reports, enforces revocations and follows the [fencing rule]" / "A replica without word from a leader for one election timeout (hypothesis) is stale"
blocking.fix: Add an 8092 class 'relay feed', served by the leader or by a non-stale replica. It streams committed entries filtered to the relay's allowed Clusters: plan and assignment state with `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq`, signed promotions, revocations, anchor sets and `clusterNodeCount`. It resumes from the relay's last applied position, or sends a full state snapshot when that position is older than the retained log. It also carries the serving replica's last leader-contact time, so the relay's staleness is (time since the replica last heard from the leader) plus (time since the relay last heard from the replica), judged against the same election-timeout bound (hypothesis). Bound its queue and state what happens on overflow: resync. Add the class to replica role 5 and to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15.

non_blocking.suggestion: A follower that still receives leader heartbeats but whose applied index is behind is not 'stale' under the fencing rule. It can send a reconnecting Node an assignment that the leader has since superseded, for example a batch assignment that a rollback overtook. The Node's fence accepts it because its sequence is higher than the Node's last activated one. The exposure lasts only as long as the replication lag, but that lag is unbounded while a snapshot installs. Define staleness also as applied index behind the leader's commit index by more than a bound, or make a follower send new configuration only after a read-index barrier.

Replica role 5 puts all 8092 classes under one 64 MiB/s per-peer cap. If Raft shares that cap, or a connection, with content replication, a large Revision can delay Raft heartbeats past the 1000 ms timeout and trigger needless elections. Say that each class uses its own connections and that the cap applies to content replication and relay feeds, never to Raft.

During a full quorum loss every replica is stale. With 'After 30 s stale (target) it sends Reconnect', every Node then reconnects repeatedly to other stale replicas for the whole outage. Send `Reconnect` only when a peer replica reports a leader, or at most once per stream.

Say where session state lives. The Raft rows of the data table list users, bindings and API token hashes but no sessions, and the memory row no longer lists them. The 30-minute idle timeout needs last-activity state that every replica can see. State one mechanism, for example session records written to Raft with the login audit entry plus a signed last-activity cookie that the serving replica refreshes, and add it to the data table.

'20 Snapshots/s (hypothesis)' needs a Snapshot size. At 50 MiB it means about 1 GB/s of egress per replica, and the 256 MiB budget allows five such Snapshots in flight. State the size behind the hypothesis, for example the median encoded Revision, and give the 5-minute batch target as a function of size.

Rotation step 2 re-signs 'each Cluster's assignment', but during a Rollout a Cluster has two live assignments: canary or batch Nodes on the new digest and the rest on the old one. Say that each distinct live assignment is re-signed at its own next sequence, or that rotation waits until no Rollout is active.

Audit batches go through Raft every 250 ms, and Raft entries must stay under 64 KiB (target). Say that a batch that would exceed the entry cap is split into several entries, so a burst of writes or logins cannot produce one oversized entry.

The ACK timeout starts at the last byte a follower writes. State that followers include that send time in status forwarding, and that Acks and Nacks received while the replica has no leader are buffered, bounded, until a leader returns.

blocking.issue: The L3-12 fix introduced a regression: key rotation now reads as if Ruralz Control can do it alone, and that contradicts the Keys row. The previous step 1 said the new key arrives 'in a root-signed `TrustUpdate`'. The new step 1 says Rotate key 'publish[es] the new key in a higher `version`'. But anchor sets carry the online keys, and 'only a trust-root key outside Ruralz Control' signs them. Rotate key (an `admin` action) therefore cannot publish anything until someone signs the new public key offline with the root and uploads the resulting anchor set. The API gives that upload to `security-admin`, a different role. The text never says how the new public key is exported for root signing, which role uploads the signed set, or that step 1 waits for the upload. Emergency removal ('publishes a higher `version` and re-signs at once') has the same gap. An operator cannot carry out a rotation from this section, and a contributor cannot implement the Rotate key action.

blocking.section: Ruralz Console / RBAC and SSO; Open questions (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9)
blocking.issue: Residual. Separation of duties for Git commits depends on the commit's author and committer email, and anyone can set that email. OQ-9 keeps option (a), no commit-signature verification, and OQ-7 keeps option (a), no forge adapters, so Ruralz Control cannot tell who actually wrote or merged a commit. The attack: an `approver` who can merge authors a malicious commit under a colleague's email and merges it, which works where forge admins bypass branch protection. The approver's own verified email does not match, so RZ-CP-007 never fires and they approve their own prod change. The reverse attack also works. Commits spoofing every approver's email make RZ-CP-007 block all approvals, which stalls prod promotions, security fixes included. Security and identity has already answered OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9 with option (b), and this document still shows (a) as current.
blocking.evidence: Line 477: "Approvers cannot approve a change they authored, committed (by verified email), wrote back, pushed, started or requested (`RZ-CP-007`, audited)". Line 603: "OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9 | Verify Git commit signatures? | (a) No (current); (b) optionally". 08-security-and-identity.md line 472: "For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-9, option (b): verify commit signatures where approvals depend on authorship".
blocking.fix: Adopt OQ-9 option (b) where `requireApproval` is set. Commit-based separation of duties uses only identities from verified commit signatures (author key bound to a Console user) or from forge adapter merge metadata. An unsigned or unverifiable commit is treated as authored by every approver-eligible user except those who explicitly attest otherwise, or requires two approvers. Say that a spoofed email can never block an approval by itself. Update the OQ-9 row to 'answered (b) by Security and identity' and add the spoofing case to the 'Compromised Git account' threat row.

blocking.section: Bundle, Revision and Rollout lifecycle / Revision signing and verification (Rotation, emergency removal); Control Store and high availability / Fencing stale replicas; Audit and security
blocking.issue: Residual regression introduced by the new fence. An online key can sign any `assignmentSeq` and `promotionSeq`. The FSM enforces 'current plus one' only on the legitimate leader, and Nodes accept any higher pair within the current `storeEpoch`. An attacker who holds the stolen online key and has a delivery path signs an assignment and a promotion with a near-maximum sequence. Delivery paths the document admits: a stolen key-encryption key, which also yields the server CA key for 8091 impersonation; a compromised relay forwarding attacker-signed messages; or a compromised replica. Nodes activate the malicious Revision, promote it to Last-Known-Good and persist the huge sequence. Emergency removal then 'publishes a higher `version` and re-signs at once' at 'the next sequences'. Nothing says it opens a new `storeEpoch`, so every legitimate re-signed assignment is lower than the persisted pair and gets a transient NACK. Affected Nodes stay on the attacker's Revision and are quarantined. Under OQ-24 option (a) they also keep booting it as Last-Known-Good. The 'Stolen online key' and 'Stolen key-encryption key' threat rows claim recovery that the fence prevents. Promotions compare 'promotionSeq only', so the same lock applies to Last-Known-Good promotion, and after a restore that opens a new epoch.
blocking.evidence: Line 248: "Emergency removal publishes a higher `version` and re-signs at once, awaiting no ACK". Line 497: "Nodes persist the highest pair activated ... compare pairs in order and send a transient NACK for a lower one ... Promotions compare `promotionSeq` only with the last accepted promotion". Line 246: "a Last-Known-Good verified before an emergency removal still boots (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24)". Line 580: "Stolen online key | ... a higher `version` removes the key". Line 581: "Stolen key-encryption key | Exposes online and CA keys: rotate the online key, Node CA and server CA".
blocking.fix: State that every emergency removal, and every server CA replacement, is a root-signed anchor set that opens a higher `storeEpoch`. Nodes compare both assignments and promotions as (`storeEpoch`, sequence) pairs, so a new epoch resets the attacker-inflated high-water marks. An emergency-removal anchor set carries a 'compromised since' time. After accepting it, a Node refuses to boot, as Last-Known-Good, any candidate or Last-Known-Good whose assignment or promotion was signed by the removed key after that time. Such a Node boots not ready or waits for the Control Stream, which amends OQ-24 for this case. Add the fence reset and this Last-Known-Good rule to the 'Stolen online key' and 'Stolen key-encryption key' threat rows.

blocking.section: GitOps model; Responsibilities and non-responsibilities; Audit and security
blocking.issue: Residual. The CRD source is now off by default, bound per namespace, audited and reported as Drift. The document still never says whether CRD-sourced Revisions pass `promotion.from` and `requireApproval`. For `ruralz bundle push` it states that promotion gating applies and that push is off by default under `requireApproval`. For CRDs it says nothing, and a CRD-sourced Revision has no commit, which is what promotion moves. The attack: once an operator binds a Kubernetes namespace to `prod`, any Kubernetes principal with write access to `ruralz.io` objects in that namespace can remove an `auth.*` Policy or widen a Plugin Capability. Those principals are often a broad namespace-admin group or a CI service account. The change then reaches prod with no `approver` and no separation of duties, only an after-the-fact Drift alert. That defeats the promise that `requireApproval` gates every prod Rollout.
blocking.evidence: Line 34: "Builds signed Revisions per Environment from Git, `ruralz bundle push` or opted-in CRDs". Line 186: "records the source tree digest in place of a commit, so promotion gating applies ... Push is per-Environment, off by default under `requireApproval`" (said for push only). Line 570: "The CRD source is off unless process configuration binds a namespace to an Environment." Line 439: "Git divergence | ... pushed Bundle or CRD source ... | Alert only, never reverted". Line 583: "CRDs bound, audited, reported as Drift".
blocking.fix: State that a CRD-sourced Revision records the digest of its source object set in place of a commit and passes `promotion.from` and `requireApproval` exactly like a pushed Bundle. Separation of duties treats the Kubernetes user as the author. By default, refuse a namespace binding to an Environment that sets `requireApproval`, mirroring push, and audit any override. Say whether `Environment` and `Cluster` CRDs are ever read. If they are, gate-relaxing changes made through them follow the same approval rule as `control/`.
